question: Under Mill's principle of liberty, may someone forcibly stop a person who is about to cross a bridge known to be unsafe? Explain when force is allowed, when only a warning is, and why this does not breach his liberty; and say to whom Mill says the principle does not apply at all.

question: Which official must initial a merchant's books before anything is written in them, and which book is exempt? Compare the 1303 Commercial Code with the current (1311) one.
reference: In both, all books of Art. 6 except the copy book must be initialled before use; the copy book needs only numbered pages. The signatory differs: 1303 - the president of the commercial court, another judge, a prosecution officer or the local governor (Art. 11); 1311 - a representative of the registration office (Art. 11).
answer:
قانون تجارت ۱۳۰۳ - ماده ۱۱: رئیس محکمه تجارت یا یکی از قضات دیگر عدلیه یا صاحب‌منصبان پارکه یا حاکم محل؛ دفتر کپیه از امضا معاف است ولی اوراق آن باید نمره ترتیبی داشته باشد.
قانون تجارت فعلی (۱۳۱۱) - ماده ۱۱: نماینده اداره‌ی ثبت (که مطابق نظام‌نامه‌ی وزارت عدلیه معین می‌شود)؛ دفتر کپیه از امضا معاف است ولی اوراق آن باید نمره‌ی ترتیبی داشته باشد.

question: Both the Digital Services Act and the Digital Markets Act use a 45 million user figure. What exactly does each Act count, and what else does the DMA require alongside that figure?

answer:
Digital Services Act - 45 million: average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union, calculated as an average over a period of six months, equivalent to 10 % of the Union population (Article 33(1), recital).
Digital Markets Act - 45 million: monthly active end users established or located in the Union in the last financial year, identified and calculated in accordance with the methodology and indicators set out in the Annex (Article 3(2)(b)).
Digital Markets Act - additional requirement: alongside the 45 million monthly active end users, the DMA requires at least 10 000 yearly active business users established in the Union, and that the thresholds in point (b) were met in each of the last three financial years (Article 3(2)(b)–(c)).

The DSA counts average monthly active recipients over six months as a proxy for societal reach (10 % of the Union population), while the DMA counts monthly active end users in the last financial year and additionally requires 10 000 yearly active business users and persistence of the thresholds over the last three financial years.
